incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: High p99 streaming tail for hosted endpoints affecting kv-cache heavy workloads
maya: seeing p99 up to 2.1s on streaming for customer-prod-5, p95 up ~200ms
sam: confirmed, dashboard shows sudden spike after kernel rollout at 03:12 UTC
liam: which kernel? TRT8+FlashAttn opt was rolled at 03:10
maya: yes, rollout id r-2026-03-15-kernel-trt8-flashattn
katie: customers affected: corp-alpha and beta, 3% of requests but big tail
jun: attaching a short trace snippet
sam: ```
TRACE sample:
request_id: rq_abc123
decode.ms.p95: 180
decode.ms.p99: 2100
kv_page_faults: 28
kernel_version: trt8-flashattn-2026-03-15
```
maya: logs show increased page_faults and repeated KV eviction GC loops
liam: that matches a compile-path optimization that changed prefetch behavior in kv cache
katie: are we seeing OOMs? metrics only show pagefaults, no OOMs
jun: I can reproduce locally with long-context streaming and small GPU memory -> reproducible p99 spike
maya: oncall to triage: @sam @liam @katie please
sam: taking lead. immediate plan: (1) revert kernel on hot path (2) route heavy streaming customers to dedicated pool (3) tweak cache TTL
liam: repro confirmed. can we hotpatch a compiler flag to disable the prefetch optimization? I have a flag `--disable-prefetch-kv` that compiles much faster
katie: revert path prepared: rollback artifact trt8-flashattn -> trt8-flashattn-prev (canary already tested)
sam: executing rollback on canary region now
ops-bot: deploy started: rollback trt8-flashattn -> trt8-flashattn-prev (canary) [link]
maya: routing rule ready: route corp-alpha and corp-beta to dedicated-pool-3
jun: applying route now using `redwoodctl route apply` snippet:
```
redwoodctl route apply --selector=customer in (corp-alpha,corp-beta) --pool=dedicated-pool-3 --priority=100
```
sam: route applied
ops-bot: canary rollback succeeded in us-east-1-canary (3/3 tasks healthy)
liam: compiling hotpatch with `--disable-prefetch-kv` now, will push to canary after smoke
katie: adding temporary autoscale buffer +20% on dedicated-pool-3
maya: early signals: p99 for corp-alpha dropped from ~2.1s to 580ms in canary
sam: starting global rollback across streaming fleet
ops-bot: rollback job queued across regions: us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-south-1
jun: note: we saw degraded throughput for a minute after rollback due to cache warmup
liam: plan for next steps post-mitigation: (A) block the problematic compile flag until tests added (B) run long-context streaming perf tests in CI, (C) postmortem and customer comms
katie: customer-impact doc draft: corp-alpha saw 9% error-like degraded responses, corp-beta p99 x4 for ~3h
maya: opening support ticket for corp-alpha with mitigations summary and ETA
sam: oncall handoff in 2h, leaving runbook notes below
sam: RUNBOOK NOTES:
1) if p99 >1.0s: route heavy customers to dedicated pool
2) if page_faults > 10/min: rollback kernel variant
3) to hotpatch compile flags: use build-worker `compile-quick` with flag `--disable-prefetch-kv`
4) escalate to eng-runtime if rollback fails
katie: adding followup tasks to eng-sre board: disable-flag-test, add-ci-hotstream
maya: :thumbsup: nice quick action
liam: sysdig trace and flamegraph attached in thread link
sam: setting severity to Sev3 -> investigating customer impact and mitigation complete
ops-bot: incident updated: status=mitigated, mitigation=rollback+routing, severity=Sev3
maya: will schedule postmortem for tomorrow 10:00 UTC
jun: thanks everyone, monitoring for 2h then handoff
katie: handing off to @liam for overnight watch
liam: ack, will monitor p95/p99 and follow runbook
sam: thanks team, closing thread after handoff
